sentences.en: Hello, everybody, and welcome back to The Psychology of Your 20s, the podcast where we talk through some of the big life changes

sentences.en: and transitions of our 20s and what they mean for our psychology.
sentences.zh: 与转型，以及它们对我们的心理意味着什么的播客。

sentences.en: Hello, everybody.
sentences.zh: 大家好。

sentences.en: Welcome back to the show.

sentences.en: Welcome back to the podcaSt.

sentences.en: New listeners, old listeners, wherever you are in the world, it is so great to have you here back for another episode.
sentences.zh: 新听众、老听众，无论你身处世界的哪个角落，非常高兴你能回来收听又一期节目。

sentences.en: As we, of course, break down the psychology of our 20s.
sentences.zh: 正如我们当然要剖析的二十岁心理学一样。

sentences.en: Today, we're going to talk about external validation.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们要聊聊外部认同。

sentences.en: We're going to talk about external validation and why it is that we seem to spend so much of our short, precious, miraculous lives looking for approval.
sentences.zh: 我们要聊聊外部认同，以及为什么我们似乎把短暂、宝贵而奇迹般的生命中如此多的时间，都花在了寻求赞许上。

sentences.en: It's this thought that seems to like stalk us in the back of even our most confident moments.
sentences.zh: 这种想法似乎像潜伏在我们最自信时刻背后的幽灵一样追踪着我们。

sentences.en: You know, but do they like me?
sentences.zh: 你知道的，就是“他们会喜欢我吗？”

sentences.en: Am I enough?
sentences.zh: “我够好吗？”

sentences.en: Like, what are they secretly thinking about me?
sentences.zh: 就像，“他们私下里是怎么看我的？”

sentences.en: And I can't be the only one who has kind of realized how much these thoughts just like take from being able to just exist in my own timeline,
sentences.zh: 我肯定不是唯一一个意识到这些想法如何剥夺了我们在自己的时间线上、

sentences.en: in my own body, in the moment, in the things that I enjoy.
sentences.zh: 在自己的身体里、在当下、在我们喜欢的事物中单纯存在的能力的人。

sentences.en: It's like every single time I do something, there is always this thought that has to be devoted to someone else, which is honestly pretty exhausting.
sentences.zh: 这就好像每次我做点什么，总有一部分思绪必须分给别人，说实话这真的挺让人精疲力竭的。

sentences.en: In our 20s, I think we are particularly susceptible to the hunger and the need for external validation.
sentences.zh: 在二十几岁的时候，我认为我们尤其容易对外部认同产生渴望和需求。

sentences.en: It is a decade of first jobs, first startup relationships, first time living independently.
sentences.zh: 这是一个充满第一份工作、第一段初试啼声的恋爱关系、第一次独立生活的十年。

sentences.en: And because everything feels uncertain, sometimes it feels like we just keep looking to our left, keep looking to others, looking over our shoulder,
sentences.zh: 而且因为一切都充满不确定性，有时感觉我们只会不停地向左看，不断看着别人，越过肩膀张望，

sentences.en: looking for someone to like give us a sign or give us some sense of guidance that we are getting it right, that we ourselves are right.
sentences.zh: 寻找某人给我们一个信号，或者给我们某种方向感，证明我们做对了，证明我们本身就是对的。

sentences.en: And don't get me wrong, you know, validation feels good.
sentences.zh: 别误会我的意思，你知道的，认同感感觉很好。

sentences.en: There's like a rush, a warmth, like a sense of being seen.
sentences.zh: 那种感觉就像是一阵涌动、一丝温暖、一种被看见的感觉。

sentences.en: But it's how much we rely on that feeling that actually makes a difference.
sentences.zh: 但我们对这种感觉的依赖程度才是真正产生差异的关键。

sentences.en: When we rely on others to tell us we're worthy, we basically hand over the keys to our self-esteem and say like, do whatever you want with this.
sentences.zh: 当我们依赖别人来告诉我们自己是有价值的，我们基本上就把自尊的钥匙交了出去，并说道：随你们怎么处置吧。

sentences.en: You know, every compliment or moment of praise can be kind of make or break.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，每一次赞美或表扬的时刻都可能是成败的关键。

sentences.en: And every critique is like a threat to a much deeper part of who we are.
sentences.zh: 而每一次批评都像是对我们更深层内心的威胁。

sentences.en: And that is what we're going to talk about today.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们今天要讨论的内容。

sentences.en: It can be addictive, but external validation is remarkably fragile as many people who have had it and lost it will tell you.
sentences.zh: 它可能会让人上瘾，但正如许多曾经拥有它又失去它的人所说的那样，外部认同是极其脆弱的。

sentences.en: And it can leave us feeling deeply hollow if and when, because it is a situation of when it disappears.
sentences.zh: 如果它消失了——而且鉴于这是一种“当”它消失而非“如果”的情况——它会让我们感到内心空洞。

sentences.en: So in this episode, we're going to break down why it actually feels so good, why some part of us really needs it, but then also how we can shift back towards internal validation.
sentences.zh: 所以在本期节目中，我们将剖析为什么它感觉如此美妙，为什么我们内心的一部分确实需要它，以及我们如何能够转向内部认同。

sentences.en: What are the hidden costs of relying on this a little bit too much?
sentences.zh: 过度依赖这个东西，隐藏的代价是什么？

sentences.en: How does people's experience with fame tell us about external validation and social approval?
sentences.zh: 人们的名人经历告诉了我们关于外部认同和社会赞许的什么？

sentences.en: And what does it do to our internal compass?
sentences.zh: 当别人的声音总是被允许压倒我们自己的声音时，它会对我们的内在罗盘产生什么影响？

sentences.en: What does it do to our values?
sentences.zh: 它会对我们的价值观产生什么影响？

sentences.en: What does it do to our authentic nature when other people's voices are always allowed to speak over our own?
sentences.zh: 它会对我们的本真天性产生什么影响？

sentences.en: I'm super excited for this episode.
sentences.zh: 我超级期待这一期节目。

sentences.en: Thank you for tuning in.
sentences.zh: 谢谢大家的收听。

sentences.en: Without further ado, let's get into why we crave external validation as much as we do.
sentences.zh: 闲话少说，让我们来探讨一下为什么我们对外部认同会有如此强烈的渴望。

sentences.en: So you've probably heard about external and internal validation as like two sides of the same coin, two distinct ways we build our sense of self-worth.
sentences.zh: 所以你可能听说过外部认同和内部认同就像一枚硬币的两面，是我们建立自我价值感的两种不同方式。

sentences.en: Whilst both feel really good and are completely necessary as well, we're not trying to like villainize external validation or make it seem unimportant.
sentences.zh: 虽然两者感觉都非常好，而且也完全是必要的——我们并不是想把外部认同妖魔化或显得它不重要——

sentences.en: They do come from very different sources and they have vastly different impacts on our long-term well-being.
sentences.zh: 但它们确实来自截然不同的源头，并且对我们的长期幸福感有着截然不同的影响。

sentences.en: So what is the difference?
sentences.zh: 那么有什么区别呢？

sentences.en: It's in the name.
sentences.zh: 答案就在字里行间。

sentences.en: External validation is any kind of affirmation that comes from the outside, specifically that comes from others.
sentences.zh: 外部认同是任何来自外部、特别是来自他人的肯定。

sentences.en: It operates on a bit of a social feedback loop whereby when someone likes a photo of yours or you experience public praise or someone saying good job
sentences.zh: 它在某种社会反馈循环中运作：当有人喜欢你的照片，或者你经历公开的表扬，或者有人说干得好，

sentences.en: or someone allowing you into the in-group, that kind of signals that others not only see us, they approve of us, which therefore makes us feel good
sentences.zh: 或者有人允许你进入核心圈子，这就在某种程度上表明别人不仅看到了我们，而且赞许我们，这因此让我们感觉良好，

sentences.en: and makes us feel like we are doing something right.
sentences.zh: 并让我们觉得自己做对了什么。

sentences.en: Think of it kind of like a signal from the outside world confirming your value and therefore your broader acceptance.
sentences.zh: 你可以把它想象成来自外部世界的一个信号，它证实了你的价值，从而证实了你获得更广泛的接纳。

sentences.en: That obviously gives us a little bit of a glow.
sentences.zh: 这显然会让我们感到容光焕发。

sentences.en: However, the problem is that the source of our worth, when it is completely external, it also means it's completely outside of our control.
sentences.zh: 然而，问题在于，当我们价值的源头完全来自外部时，这也意味着它完全超出了我们的控制。

sentences.en: Even though we can like dictate our actions to try and gain more validation, there's actually no determining whether we will actually receive it from our desired target.
sentences.zh: 尽管我们可以通过支配自己的行为来试图获得更多认同，但实际上没有任何因素能决定我们是否真的能从心仪的目标那里得到它。

sentences.en: Therefore, it is what we call a borrowed or inconstant sense of value that by its very nature can be given or taken away by others at any time and more specifically for any reason,
sentences.zh: 因此，这就是我们所说的借来的或不稳定的价值感，它本质上可以随时被别人给予或剥夺，更具体地说，可以出于任何原因，

sentences.en: fair or unfair.
sentences.zh: 公平或不公平。

sentences.en: Internal validation, however, is different.
sentences.zh: 然而，内部认同则不同。

sentences.en: It comes from within.
sentences.zh: 它发自内心。

sentences.en: Its source is from ourselves.
sentences.zh: 它的源头是我们自己。

sentences.en: It's your ability to recognize your own worth, your own effort, integrity, your own beauty and specialness and intelligence, regardless of whether others react
sentences.zh: 它是你无论别人作何反应，都能认识到自己的价值、自己的努力、正直、美丽、独特性和智慧的能力，

sentences.en: the way that you want them to.
sentences.zh: 无论别人是否如你所愿地做出反应。

sentences.en: This type of validation is not about an outcome.
sentences.zh: 这种认同无关乎结果。

sentences.en: It's not specifically about praise.
sentences.zh: 它不仅仅关乎表扬。

sentences.en: It's not specifically about social approval.
sentences.zh: 它也不仅仅关乎社会赞许。

sentences.en: It's about self-approval and self-assessment.
sentences.zh: 它是关于自我赞许和自我评估。

sentences.en: For example, you know, instead of waiting for someone to read an article you wrote or look at something you're really proud of and acknowledge that for you,
sentences.zh: 例如，你知道的，与其等着别人去阅读你写的一篇文章或看一眼你引以为豪的东西并为你给予认可，

sentences.en: you are able to acknowledge your hard work independently.
sentences.zh: 你能够独立地认可自己的辛勤工作。

sentences.en: You are able to kind of put on your objective lenses and say, hey, that actually took a lot of time for me.
sentences.zh: 你能够戴上有色眼镜客观看待并说，嘿，那其实花了我很多时间。

sentences.en: That actually is and does show real talent for me.
sentences.zh: 那实际上确实展现并体现了我的真正天赋。

sentences.en: I'm allowed to be proud of that, even if my contributions and my effort goes unnoticed by other people.
sentences.zh: 我允许自己为之骄傲，即使我的贡献和努力没有被其他人注意到。

sentences.en: I think sometimes we have like a natural instinct against this because as much as we want social approval, we also don't want to come off as arrogant.
sentences.zh: 我想有时我们对此会有自然的抗拒心理，因为尽管我们渴望社会赞许，但我们也不想表现得傲慢自大。

sentences.en: And for a lot of cultures, individualistic or collective, like humility is something that we prize and praise beyond anything else.
sentences.zh: 对于许多文化来说，无论是个人主义还是集体主义，谦逊都是我们高于一切去珍视和赞美的品质。

sentences.en: Having internal validation doesn't mean that you are like an egomaniac.
sentences.zh: 拥有内部认同并不意味着你是一个利己狂。

sentences.en: It just means that you actually are able to be honest about your own skills, about your own effort, about your own internal worth.
sentences.zh: 这只意味着你确实能够诚实地看待自己的技能、自己的努力以及你内心的价值。

sentences.en: Like humility is sometimes just as dishonest
sentences.zh: 就像谦逊有时和傲慢一样，

sentences.en: as arrogance.
sentences.zh: 是不诚实的表现。

sentences.en: So internal validation and a sense of strong internal self-worth, I think when done right, is like one of the most honest ways we can show up in society and the most honest ways
sentences.zh: 因此，内部认同和强烈的内在自我价值感，我认为如果做得对，是我们融入社会最诚实的方式之一，也是我们对待自己的最诚实方式

sentences.en: we can approach ourselves.
sentences.zh: 我们可以采用的方法。

sentences.en: The difference really comes down to this.
sentences.zh: 区别其实归结于这一点。

sentences.en: External validation really asks, do they think I'm okay?
sentences.zh: 外部认同真正问的是：他们觉得我好吗？

sentences.en: And internal validation asks, do I think I'm okay?
sentences.zh: 而内部认同问的是：我觉得自己好吗？

sentences.en: Think about someone that's just been on a first date.
sentences.zh: 想象一下刚刚经历第一次约会的人。

sentences.en: Someone reliant on external validation may start thinking, you know, I really wonder what they thought of me.
sentences.zh: 依赖外部认同的人可能会开始想，你知道的，我真想知道他们是怎么看我的。

sentences.en: I really wonder if they liked my outfit.
sentences.zh: 我真想知道他们是否喜欢我的穿着。
